+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = "") -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config
+        self.config = config
+        self.vocab_size = config.vocab_size
+        self.num_redundant_experts = (
+            vllm_config.parallel_config.eplb_config.num_redundant_experts
+        )
+        self.attn_res_block_size = get_attn_res_block_size(config)
+        self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(
+            num_embeddings=config.vocab_size, embedding_dim=config.hidden_size
+        )
+
+        def get_layer(prefix: str) -> AliceAIDecoderBlock:
+            return AliceAIDecoderBlock(
+                vllm_config=vllm_config,
+                layer_type=config.layer_types[extract_layer_index(prefix)],
+                prefix=prefix,
+            )
+
+        self.start_layer, self.end_layer, self.layers = make_layers(
+            num_hidden_layers=config.num_hidden_layers,
+            layer_fn=get_layer,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.layers",
+        )
+        self.is_fused_shared_expert_enabled = is_model_fused_shared_expert_compatible(
+            layers=self.layers, moe_cls=AliceAISparseMoeBlock, moe_name="mlp"
+        )
+        self.norm = GemmaRMSNorm(
+            hidden_size=config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps
+        )
+        self.attnres_final = _AttentionResidualFinal(
+            hidden_size=config.hidden_size,
+            rms_norm_eps=float(config.rms_norm_eps),
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.attnres_final",
+        )
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
+
+    def _init_residual_bank(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        residual_bank = hidden_states.new_empty(
+            (
+                hidden_states.shape[0],
+                (self.config.num_hidden_layers + self.attn_res_block_size - 1)
+                // self.attn_res_block_size,
+                hidden_states.shape[-1],
+            )
+        )
+        residual_bank[:, 0].copy_(hidden_states)
+        return residual_bank
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | IntermediateTensors:
+        if intermediate_tensors is not None:
+            raise NotImplementedError("AliceAI does not support pipeline parallelism")
+        if not get_pp_group().is_first_rank or not get_pp_group().is_last_rank:
+            raise NotImplementedError("AliceAI requires pipeline_parallel_size=1")
+
+        if inputs_embeds is not None:
+            hidden_states = inputs_embeds
+        else:
+            assert input_ids is not None
+            hidden_states = self.embed_input_ids(input_ids)
+        residual_bank = self._init_residual_bank(hidden_states)
+
+        num_completed_sources = 1
+        partial = None
+        for layer in islice(self.layers, self.start_layer, self.end_layer):
+            num_completed_sources, partial = layer.forward_attn_res(
+                positions=positions,
+                residual_bank=residual_bank,
+                num_completed_sources=num_completed_sources,
+                partial=partial,
+            )
+        if partial is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("AttnRes produced an empty final block")
+        hidden_states = self.attnres_final(
+            residual_bank=residual_bank,
+            num_completed_sources=num_completed_sources,
+            partial=partial,
+        )
+        return self.norm(hidden_states)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        weights = maybe_fuse_shared_experts(
+            weights=weights,
+            enabled=self.is_fused_shared_expert_enabled,
+            n_routed_experts=self.config.num_experts,
+            n_shared_experts=1,
+            ckpt_prefix="mlp.shared_expert",
+        )
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(self)
+        return loader.load_weights(weights=weights, mapper=self.hf_to_vllm_mapper)
+
+
+class AliceAIForCausalLM(
+    nn.Module, HasInnerState, IsHybrid, SupportsLoRA, MixtureOfExperts

+    hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper(orig_to_new_prefix={"mtp.": None})

+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self.model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        self.scheduler_config = vllm_config.scheduler_config
+        self.quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+        self.config = config
+        self.model = AliceAIModel(
+            vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "model")
+        )
+        self.lm_head = ParallelLMHead(
+            num_embeddings=config.vocab_size,
+            embedding_dim=config.hidden_size,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "lm_head"),
+        )
+        self.logits_processor = LogitsProcessor(config.vocab_size)
+        self.set_moe_parameters()
+
+    def set_moe_parameters(self) -> None:
+        self.moe_layers = [layer.mlp.experts for layer in self.model.layers]
+        moe = self.model.layers[self.model.start_layer].mlp
+        self.num_moe_layers = len(self.moe_layers)
+        self.num_expert_groups = 1
+        self.num_shared_experts = 0
+        self.num_logical_experts = moe.n_logical_experts
+        self.num_physical_experts = moe.n_physical_experts
+        self.num_local_physical_experts = moe.n_local_physical_experts
+        self.num_routed_experts = moe.n_routed_experts
+        self.num_redundant_experts = moe.n_redundant_experts

+    def update_physical_experts_metadata(
+        self,

+        num_local_physical_experts: int,

+        self.num_physical_experts = num_physical_experts
+        self.num_local_physical_experts = num_local_physical_experts
+        self.num_redundant_experts = num_physical_experts - self.num_logical_experts
+        for layer in self.model.layers:
+            moe = layer.mlp
+            moe.n_local_physical_experts = num_local_physical_experts
+            moe.n_physical_experts = num_physical_experts
+            moe.n_redundant_experts = self.num_redundant_experts
+            moe.experts.update_expert_map()
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.model.embed_input_ids(input_ids)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        **kwargs: object,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | IntermediateTensors:

+            intermediate_tensors=intermediate_tensors,

+
+    def compute_logits(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:

+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config(

+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_mamba_state_shape_from_config(

+        return MambaStateShapeCalculator.kda_state_shape(

+            num_heads=config.linear_num_key_heads,
+            head_dim=config.linear_key_head_dim,

+    @classmethod

+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from vllm.renderers.chat_utils import ConversationMessage, parse_chat_message_content
+
+
+def _parse_one(message) -> ConversationMessage:
+    # Plain-text content only reads these two tracker attributes.
+    tracker = MagicMock()
+    parser = tracker.create_parser.return_value
+    parser.model_config.enable_prompt_embeds = False
+    parser.mm_placeholder_storage.return_value = {}
+    result = parse_chat_message_content(
+        message, tracker, content_format="string", interleave_strings=False
+    )
+    assert len(result) == 1
+    return result[0]
+
+
+def test_assistant_reasoning_is_mirrored_to_reasoning_content():
+    """``reasoning`` is mirrored to ``reasoning_content`` for legacy templates."""
+    conv_msg = _parse_one(
+        {
+            "role": "assistant",
+            "content": "4",
+            "reasoning": "2+2 equals 4",
+        }
+    )
+
+    assert conv_msg.get("reasoning") == "2+2 equals 4"
+    assert conv_msg.get("reasoning_content") == "2+2 equals 4"
+
+
+def test_assistant_without_reasoning_sets_neither_field():
+    """No reasoning in, no reasoning keys out: no empty thinking block in templates."""
+    conv_msg = _parse_one({"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi"})
+
+    assert "reasoning" not in conv_msg
+    assert "reasoning_content" not in conv_msg
+
+
+def test_non_assistant_reasoning_is_not_mirrored():
+    """Only assistant turns carry reasoning; a user turn must not."""
+    conv_msg = _parse_one(
+        {"role": "user", "content": "Hi", "reasoning": "should be ignored"}
+    )
+
+    assert "reasoning" not in conv_msg
+    assert "reasoning_content" not in conv_msg

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+import asyncio
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.renderers.chat_utils import AsyncMultiModalItemTracker
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_resolve_items_runs_modalities_concurrently_and_preserves_order():
+    """Media fetches overlap while modality and item order are preserved."""
+    active_fetches = 0
+    max_active_fetches = 0
+
+    async def _fetch(name: str, delay: float):
+        nonlocal active_fetches, max_active_fetches
+        active_fetches += 1
+        max_active_fetches = max(max_active_fetches, active_fetches)
+        try:
+            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
+            return name, f"{name}-uuid"
+        finally:
+            active_fetches -= 1
+
+    tracker = AsyncMultiModalItemTracker(MagicMock(is_multimodal_model=True))
+    tracker.__dict__["mm_processor"] = MagicMock()
+    tracker._items_by_modality["video"] = [
+        lambda: _fetch("video-0", 0.02),
+        lambda: _fetch("video-1", 0.01),
+    ]
+    tracker._items_by_modality["image"] = [
+        lambda: _fetch("image-0", 0.02),
+        lambda: _fetch("image-1", 0.01),
+    ]
+    tracker._items_by_modality["audio"] = [
+        lambda: _fetch("audio-0", 0.02),
+        lambda: _fetch("audio-1", 0.01),
+    ]
+
+    mm_data, mm_uuids = await tracker.resolve_items()
+
+    assert mm_data is not None
+    assert mm_uuids is not None
+    assert max_active_fetches == 6
+    assert list(mm_data) == ["image", "audio", "video"]
+    assert list(mm_uuids) == ["image", "audio", "video"]
+    assert mm_data == {
+        "image": ["image-0", "image-1"],
+        "audio": ["audio-0", "audio-1"],
+        "video": ["video-0", "video-1"],
+    }
+    assert mm_uuids == {
+        "image": ["image-0-uuid", "image-1-uuid"],
+        "audio": ["audio-0-uuid", "audio-1-uuid"],
+        "video": ["video-0-uuid", "video-1-uuid"],
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_resolve_items_does_not_leak_tasks_on_partial_failure():
+    """Regression test: one failing media fetch must not abandon the other
+    still-in-flight fetches across modality batches.
+
+    Before the fix, `resolve_items` gathered per-modality fetches with plain
+    `asyncio.gather`, so the first exception propagated immediately while
+    sibling fetches (real network/thread-pool work in production) kept
+    running detached, with nothing left to await or cancel them.
+    """
+
+    async def _fetch(should_fail: bool, delay: float):
+        if should_fail:
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
+            raise ValueError("simulated fetch failure")
+        await asyncio.sleep(delay)
+        return ("decoded", None)
+
+    tracker = AsyncMultiModalItemTracker(MagicMock())
+    tracker._items_by_modality["image"] = [
+        lambda: _fetch(True, 0),
+        lambda: _fetch(False, 0.2),
+        lambda: _fetch(False, 0.2),
+    ]
+    tracker._items_by_modality["audio"] = [lambda: _fetch(False, 0.2)]
+    tracker._items_by_modality["video"] = [lambda: _fetch(False, 0.2)]
+
+    tasks_before = asyncio.all_tasks()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="simulated fetch failure"):
+        await tracker.resolve_items()
+
+    leaked_tasks = asyncio.all_tasks() - tasks_before
+    assert not leaked_tasks, (
+        f"resolve_items left {len(leaked_tasks)} task(s) running after "
+        f"raising: {leaked_tasks}"
+    )

+def _assistant_tool_call(arguments, name="write"):
+    return [
+        {
+            "role": "assistant",
+            "content": "",
+            "tool_calls": [
+                {
+                    "id": "call_0",
+                    "type": "function",
+                    "function": {"name": name, "arguments": arguments},

+
+def _assistant_tool_calls(calls):

+        {
+            "role": "assistant",
+            "content": "",
+            "tool_calls": calls,
+        }
+    ]
+
+
+def test_tool_call_arguments_dict_passthrough(caplog):
+    messages = _assistant_tool_call({"a": 1})
+    _postprocess_messages(messages)
+    args = messages[0]["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["arguments"]
+    assert args == {"a": 1}
+    assert not caplog.records
+
+
+def test_tool_call_arguments_valid_object_string(caplog):

+    assert args == {"a": 1}
+    assert not caplog.records
+
+
+def test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_small(caplog):
+    bad = '{"cmd": "mkdir -p /tmp/mmadtest && cat > /tmp/mmadtest'

+    _postprocess_messages(messages)
+    args = messages[0]["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["arguments"]
+    assert args == {}
+
+    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
+    assert "coercing to an empty object" in caplog.records[0].message
+
+
+def test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_large(caplog):
+    bad = '{"filepath": "src/main.py", "contents": "' + ("x" * 18000)
+    messages = _assistant_tool_call(bad, name="write")
+    _postprocess_messages(messages)
+    args = messages[0]["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["arguments"]
+    assert args == {}
+
+    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
+    assert "coercing to an empty object" in caplog.records[0].message
+    assert f"{len(bad)} chars" in caplog.records[0].message

+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("non_obj", ["[]", "42", "true", '"hello"', "null"])
+def test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object(caplog, non_obj):

+    _postprocess_messages(messages)
+    args = messages[0]["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["arguments"]
+    assert args == {}
+
+    if non_obj == "null":
+        # null parses to None, so no warning is emitted according to requirements

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Literal
+
+from vllm.inputs import MultiModalDataDict, MultiModalUUIDDict
+
+ModalityType = Literal["image", "video", "audio"]
+MultiModalDataCounts = Mapping[ModalityType, int]
+
+
+def assert_mm_uuids(
+    mm_uuids: MultiModalUUIDDict | None,
+    media_count: int,
+    expected_uuids: list[str | None],
+    modality: str = "image",
+) -> None:
+    if len(expected_uuids) > 0:
+        assert mm_uuids is not None
+        assert modality in mm_uuids
+
+        image_uuids = mm_uuids.get(modality)
+        assert image_uuids is not None
+
+        assert isinstance(image_uuids, list) and len(image_uuids) == media_count
+
+        assert image_uuids == expected_uuids
+    else:
+        assert mm_uuids is None
+
+
+def assert_mm_data_inputs(
+    mm_data: MultiModalDataDict | None,
+    data_count: MultiModalDataCounts,
+    skipped_media_indices: dict[str, list] | None = None,  # modality -> list[int]
+) -> None:
+    assert mm_data is not None
+    assert set(data_count.keys()) == (set(mm_data.keys()))
+
+    for modality, n in data_count.items():
+        modality_data = mm_data.get(modality)
+        assert modality_data is not None
+        assert isinstance(modality_data, list) and len(modality_data) == n
+
+        if skipped_media_indices is not None:
+            skipped_media_indices_for_modality = skipped_media_indices.get(modality)
+            assert skipped_media_indices_for_modality is not None
+            for i in skipped_media_indices_for_modality:
+                assert modality_data[i] is None
+
+
+def assert_mm_data_is_image_input(
+    mm_data: MultiModalDataDict | None,
+    image_count: int,
+    skipped_image_indices: list | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    assert mm_data is not None
+    assert set(mm_data.keys()) == {"image"}
+
+    image_data = mm_data.get("image")
+    assert image_data is not None
+
+    assert isinstance(image_data, list) and len(image_data) == image_count
+    if skipped_image_indices is not None:
+        for i in skipped_image_indices:
+            assert image_data[i] is None

@@ -121,20 +121,25 @@ For each deleted config:
 Deleted processors follow the same steps in
 `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/__init__.py`.
 
+Before merging, rebase and grep again for the old field names: PRs that land
+in between still read them.
+
 Done when every line of the inventory output is deleted, or kept with a
 reason that meets the bar in step 2. The PR also carries the config diff
 results and evals for any changed values.
 
 ## Upstreaming hazards
 
 Upstream configs are `@strict` dataclasses. Checkpoint keys upstream does not
-declare survive as plain attributes. Defaults that only vLLM sets, and values
-vLLM derives, vanish.
+declare survive as plain attributes, but only when the checkpoint sets them.
+Defaults that only vLLM sets, and values vLLM derives, vanish.
 
 | Hazard | Signal | Fix |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | Upstream consumes legacy keys | `__post_init__` pops keys the model reads (`deepseek_v4` `compress_ratios`) | Read the upstream replacement (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-layer `rope_parameters`) |
 | Renamed or dropped fields | Diff shows `<MISSING>` for a field the model reads | Read the upstream name; derive dropped flags from what implies them (`enable_moe_block` from `num_experts`) |
+| Undeclared field without a default | `config.x` raises `AttributeError` for configs that omit `x`, e.g. minimal test configs (A.X-K1 `scoring_func`). Dumps of real checkpoints miss it | Upstream ignoring `x` usually means vLLM can stop reading it; if vLLM truly needs it, read `getattr(config, "x", <old default>)` |
+| Top-level config stops forwarding | The vendored top-level config forwarded reads to `text_config`; upstream does not. `getattr(config, "x", default)` silently takes the default, e.g. on MTP draft configs from `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`, which the dumps do not build | Read from `get_text_config()`; grep `getattr` reads of every field, including speculative-decoding paths |
 | Type check on the config | `ctx.get_hf_config(SomeConfig)` relies on the vendored base class | Accept the upstream class too, e.g. a `Cosmos3ProcessingInfo` overriding `get_hf_config` |
 | Remote code takes over | Checkpoint `config.json` has `auto_map`; with `--trust-remote-code`, the hub class replaces the native one once vLLM stops registering its own | Check the remote class loads; if not, register the upstream class for that `model_type` |
 | Read-only upstream fields | Properties or derived fields break subclasses and `hf_overrides` (`nemotron_h` `hybrid_override_pattern`) | Override the source field (`layers_block_type`) instead |

+    layers. Returns an empty list for other configs.

+        return compress_ratios
+    if (compress_rates := getattr(config, "compress_rates", None)) is None:
+        return []

 ### Which `dtype` should be used?
 
 - Currently, vLLM CPU uses model default settings as `dtype`. However, due to unstable float16 support in torch CPU, it is recommended to explicitly set `dtype=bfloat16` if there are any performance or accuracy problem.  
-- On AMD Zen CPUs (`ZenCpuPlatform`), `float16` is **not** supported. Only `bfloat16` and `float32` are accepted; models declared with `float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at model load time. See [AMD Zen optimizations](#amd-zen-optimizations).
+- On AMD Zen CPUs (`ZenCpuPlatform`), `float16` requires AVX512-FP16, available from Venice (6th Gen EPYC) onwards. On Turin (5th Gen EPYC) and earlier only `bfloat16` and `float32` are accepted, and models declared with `float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at model load time. See [AMD Zen optimizations](#amd-zen-optimizations).
 
 ### How to launch a vLLM service on CPU?

@@ -273,7 +273,9 @@ Otherwise, vLLM falls back to the default `CpuPlatform` (oneDNN / sgl-kernel pat
 
 ### Supported dtypes
 
-`float16` is **not** supported on `ZenCpuPlatform`. `ZenCpuPlatform.supported_dtypes` advertises only `bfloat16` and `float32`, so models declared with `torch_dtype=float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at load time with the standard `"Your device 'cpu' doesn't support torch.float16. Falling back to torch.bfloat16 for compatibility."` warning emitted from `vllm/config/model.py`.
+`ZenCpuPlatform.supported_dtypes` always advertises `bfloat16` and `float32`, and adds `float16` when `torch.ops.zentorch.zentorch_is_fp16_supported()` reports AVX512-FP16, which AMD ships from Venice (6th Gen EPYC) onwards. On Turin (5th Gen EPYC) and earlier, models declared with `torch_dtype=float16` are auto-downcast to `bfloat16` at load time with the standard `"Your device 'cpu' doesn't support torch.float16. Falling back to torch.bfloat16 for compatibility."` warning emitted from `vllm/config/model.py`.
+
+`bfloat16` is listed first either way, so `--dtype auto` keeps resolving to it.

[KV Offload] Expose OffloadingManager.lock()/unlock() and service the tiering control plane off the scheduler thread (#58168)

Signed-off-by: Liran Schour <lirans@il.ibm.com>
Co-authored-by: Kevin H. Luu <khluu000@gmail.com>

@@ -108,6 +108,7 @@ vllm serve <model> \
 | `store_threshold` | no | `0` | single-tier | Min lookups before a block is offloaded. Values ≥ 2 are rejected by `TieringOffloadingSpec`. |
 | `max_tracker_size` | no | `64000` | single-tier | Max entries in the lookup tracker. |
 | `secondary_tiers` | no | `[]` | multi-tier | List of secondary tier configs (see below). |
+| `tier_poll_interval_s` | no | `0.001` | multi-tier | Pause between tier-poll rounds for tiers that must be serviced between engine steps (currently `p2p`). See [Threading model](#threading-model). Set to `0` to disable the thread and service those tiers once per engine step instead. |
 | `offload_prompt_only` | no | `true` | both | If `true`, only prompt (prefill) blocks are offloaded; decode blocks are skipped. |
 | `self_describing_kv_events` | no | `false` | both | Opt-in. When `true` *and* KV cache events are enabled (`--kv-events-config` with `enable_kv_cache_events`), the connector emits self-describing block-granular `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` payloads (constituent block hashes, whole-chunk `token_ids`, per-block `block_size`, parent hash, LoRA + group/cache-spec metadata) instead of the placeholder fallback, so external KV-event consumers can index offloaded blocks. Inert unless events are enabled. With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a CPU promotion is self-describing when a local request observes its primary-tier `HIT` before event translation; otherwise its stored event may retain the placeholder, while a later `HIT` can backfill metadata for removal. Pending-removal/re-promotion races and externally initiated promotions may also produce placeholders, and consumers must ignore removals for unknown hashes. Partial recurrent tails emit the hash-aligned portion from the physical block start through the tail boundary. Other sliding-window/SSM chunks keep the placeholder fallback. In chunk mode (`block_size` > GPU block size, or `blocks_per_chunk` > 1), overlapping chunks re-announce shared per-block hashes, so consumers must reference-count (deduplicate) repeated store/remove announcements. |

@@ -167,6 +168,19 @@ The filesystem and object-store tiers can publish hash-only `BlockStored` KV eve
 
 Set the optional `locality` tier field to `LOCAL` or `REMOTE` to describe the tier's storage location relative to the publishing vLLM instance. `LOCAL` marks storage local to that instance, while `REMOTE` marks storage that is not local to it. When the setting is omitted, locality is unspecified. vLLM does not infer it from the tier type, so an `obj` tier is not implicitly `REMOTE`. A KV event includes `locality` only when the tier explicitly configures it. This metadata describes the tier property without implying that a consumer can already route requests to its blocks.
 
+### Threading model
+
+Tier methods run in the scheduler process, under the tiering manager's lock, so they are never entered concurrently. They are not always called from the same thread, though.
+
+Most tiers only ever see the scheduler thread, which holds the lock for the length of one engine step. A tier whose counterpart is not driven by the engine — the `p2p` tier, answering a remote peer — needs servicing while the engine is busy running the model, because otherwise a peer's lookup or fetch waits for the next step boundary. On a saturated rank that wait can be seconds, dwarfing the transfer it gates. Such tiers set `tolerates_off_thread_polling`, and the tiering manager runs one tier-poll thread that, once per `tier_poll_interval_s`, polls them for finished jobs and lets them serve external requests. A tier that implements `serve_external_requests()` without setting the flag is served once per engine step only.
+
+Two consequences worth knowing:
+
+- Any tier can be reached from that thread indirectly, because serving a peer looks keys up through the tiering manager, which fans out to the other tiers. Tier state must therefore not assume a particular thread, only that the manager lock is held.
+- Work the thread deliberately leaves alone is batched per step: a promotion it initiates is submitted at the next `on_schedule_end()`, not immediately.
+
+Setting `tier_poll_interval_s` to `0` disables the thread; opted-in tiers then get serviced once per engine step, as they were before it existed.
+
 ### Filesystem (FS)
 
 The filesystem tier (`type: "fs"`) writes blocks to a filesystem directory.

     --load-format runai_streamer
 ```
 
+## Model-specific checkpoint selection
+
+For models exposing `is_unused_checkpoint_weight`, `runai_streamer` skips
+safetensors files containing only unused weights before streaming. It uses the
+same model-owned rule as the default loader, including MTP draft models with
+this hook; it does not assume a particular MTP tensor prefix.
+
+Object-storage checkpoints use `model.safetensors.index.json` and verify excluded
+shards against their safetensors headers before streaming. Mixed shards remain
+included. Missing or inconsistent metadata retains the original file list.
+Models without a selection rule keep all files. Distributed streaming with
+pipeline parallelism also retains the full file list. This optimization does
+not change `runai_streamer_sharded`.
+

 You can tune parameters using `--model-loader-extra-config`:

+    assert reallocated_swa.is_valid_token[:12].all()

+    holds back the same tail: trailing whitespace, a dropped closer and a
+    partial ``STRING_DELIM``. ``STRING_DELIM`` is a special token but not a
+    lexer terminal, so unlike a tag it may reach the extender split across
+    deltas; the held tail doubles as the window that detects the close.
+    """
+    text = raw_args.strip()
+    opens, closes = text.count("("), text.count(")")
+    body = _drop_call_closer(text, opens < closes)
+    params, open_key = _parse_gemma4_fields(body, partial=True)
+    if open_key is None or next(reversed(params)) != open_key:
+        return None
+
+    held_len = (
+        len(raw_args)
+        - len(raw_args.rstrip())
+        + len(text)
+        - len(_strip_partial_delim(body))
+    )
+    held = raw_args[len(raw_args) - held_len :] if held_len else ""
+
+    def extend(delta: str) -> str | None:
+        nonlocal held, opens, closes
+        text = held + delta
+        if STRING_DELIM in text:
+            return None
+        opens += delta.count("(")
+        closes += delta.count(")")
+        visible = _strip_partial_delim(_drop_call_closer(text.rstrip(), opens < closes))
+        held = text[len(visible) :]
+        return json.dumps(visible, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
+
+    return extend
+

+_PACKED_WEIGHTS = ("w13_weight", "w2_weight")
+
+
+class CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod(Mxfp4MoEMethod):
+    """MXFP4 weights with dynamic FP8 activations in compressed-tensors format.
+
+    Only the checkpoint naming and the declared activation scheme differ from
+    the native MXFP4 path, so backend selection, weight conversion and
+    execution are inherited.
+    """
+
+    # The packed -> unpacked rename means a processed state dict no longer
+    # matches the parameters registered by create_weights.
+    supports_pre_processed_weights = False
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer: RoutedExperts, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().create_weights(layer, *args, **kwargs)
+        for name in _PACKED_WEIGHTS:

+            delattr(layer, name)
+            layer.register_parameter(f"{name}_packed", param)

+        for name in _PACKED_WEIGHTS:

+            layer.register_parameter(name, param)

+"""Compare in-tree vs AITER sparse-indexer prefill top-k at GLM-5.3-Flash shapes.
+
+Example:
+    .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_sparse_indexer_topk_prefill.py \
+        --num-rows 1024 --num-cols 131072 --topk 512
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import time
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops  # noqa: F401
+from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+
+
+def _make_inputs(num_rows, num_cols, causal, device):
+    logits = torch.randn(num_rows, num_cols, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    row_starts = torch.zeros(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if causal:
+        ramp = torch.arange(1, num_rows + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+        row_ends = (ramp * (num_cols / num_rows)).ceil().to(torch.int32)
+    else:
+        row_ends = torch.full((num_rows,), num_cols, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return logits, row_starts, row_ends
+
+
+def _time(fn, iters, warmup):
+    for _ in range(warmup):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return (time.perf_counter() - start) / iters * 1e3
+
+
+def _selected_set(indices, row_starts):
+    valid = indices >= 0
+    return [set(r[m].tolist()) for r, m in zip(indices.cpu(), valid.cpu())]
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--num-rows", type=int, default=1024)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-cols", type=int, default=131072)
+    parser.add_argument("--topk", type=int, default=512)
+    parser.add_argument("--causal", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=20)
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=5)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    logits, row_starts, row_ends = _make_inputs(
+        args.num_rows, args.num_cols, args.causal, device
+    )
+    print(
+        f"rows={args.num_rows} cols={args.num_cols} k={args.topk} "
+        f"causal={args.causal} logits={logits.numel() * 4 / 2**20:.0f} MiB "
+        f"path={os.environ.get('TOPK_FORCE_PATH', 'auto')}"
+    )
+
+    native = torch.empty(args.num_rows, args.topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    def run_native():
+        torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_prefill(
+            logits,
+            row_starts,
+            row_ends,
+            native,
+            args.num_rows,
+            logits.stride(0),
+            logits.stride(1),
+            args.topk,
+        )
+
+    native_ms = _time(run_native, args.iters, args.warmup)
+    print(f"in-tree  topKPerRowPrefill : {native_ms:8.3f} ms")
+
+    if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_indexer_top_k_enabled():
+        print(
+            "AITER path unavailable: requires ROCm gfx950 with AITER installed "
+            "and VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1"
+        )
+        return
+
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        _launch_aiter_top_k_per_row_prefill,
+    )
+
+    aiter_out = torch.empty(args.num_rows, args.topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    def run_aiter():
+        _launch_aiter_top_k_per_row_prefill(
+            logits, row_starts, row_ends, aiter_out, args.topk
+        )
+
+    try:
+        aiter_ms = _time(run_aiter, args.iters, args.warmup)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        print(f"AITER path failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+        return
+    print(f"AITER    top_k_per_row_prefill: {aiter_ms:8.3f} ms")
+    print(f"speedup  : {native_ms / aiter_ms:.2f}x")
+
+    ref = _selected_set(native, row_starts)
+    got = _selected_set(aiter_out, row_starts)
+    mismatched = sum(1 for a, b in zip(ref, got) if a != b)
+    worst = max((len(a ^ b) for a, b in zip(ref, got)), default=0)
+    print(f"rows differing: {mismatched}/{args.num_rows} (worst sym-diff {worst})")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+def _to_pil_image(image: object) -> Image.Image:
+    """Convert a `uint8` array/tensor image item to PIL, since the checkpoint's
+    image processor calls `.convert("RGB")` on every input."""
+    if isinstance(image, Image.Image):
+        return image
+
+    array = image.numpy() if isinstance(image, torch.Tensor) else np.asarray(image)
+    if array.dtype != np.uint8 or array.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Nemotron-Parse expects image arrays/tensors to be 3-D uint8, "
+            f"got {array.dtype} {array.shape}"
+        )
+    # Same layout heuristic as `ImageProcessorItems.get_image_size`.
+    if array.shape[-1] not in (1, 3, 4):
+        array = array.transpose(1, 2, 0)
+    if array.shape[-1] == 1:
+        array = array[..., 0]
+
+    return Image.fromarray(np.ascontiguousarray(array))
+
+
+def _build_uint8_canvas(
+    image_processor: Any, images: Sequence[Image.Image]
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reproduce the image processor's pipeline up to, but excluding, its
+    `ToTensor` rescale, yielding the padded `uint8` canvas as `(N, 3, H, W)`.
+
+    Raises `AttributeError`/`TypeError` if the checkpoint's remote code does
+    not expose that pipeline.
+    """
+    resize = image_processor._resize_with_aspect_ratio
+    pad = image_processor._pad_to_size
+    # v1.x pads with albumentations, 2.0 sets `transform` to None and pads
+    # with `_pad_to_size`; mirror `preprocess` and pick the same branch.
+    transform = image_processor.transform
+
+    canvases = []
+    for image in images:
+        array = np.asarray(image.convert("RGB"))
+        array = resize(array)
+        array = transform(image=array)["image"] if transform is not None else pad(array)
+        if array.dtype != np.uint8 or array.ndim != 3 or array.shape[2] != 3:
+            raise TypeError(
+                f"expected a uint8 HWC canvas, got {array.dtype} {array.shape}"
+            )
+        canvases.append(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(array)).permute(2, 0, 1))
+
+    return torch.stack(canvases)
+

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+---
+name: model-microbenchmark
+description: Time a vLLM model's forward pass on exact batch shapes (decode, prefill, chunked prefill, prefix hit, spec-decode verify, or mixes) with `vllm bench forward`, single-GPU or DP/TP/EP across nodes. Use for per-step model latency, layout/parallelism comparisons, and checking a model-level optimization. Not for single kernels (use kernel-microbenchmark) or end-to-end serving (use `vllm bench serve`).
+---
+
+# Model Microbenchmark (`vllm bench forward`)
+
+Builds the batch without the scheduler, runs it through MRV2's real
+`execute_model`, and times the forward as a one-shot CUDA graph (prefill
+included). Sampling, the speculator, and CPU step overhead are excluded, so
+expect results somewhat below a serving step.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
+  --case decode=64*1@8192 --case prefill=8192 --case mix=4096,32*1@8192
+
+# DP/TP/EP: one process per GPU (multi-node: add --nnodes/--node-rank/--master-addr)
+torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
+  --model ... -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --case decode=128*1@100000
+```
+
+Requests: `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]`, comma-separated, per DP rank.
+
+| Form | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `8192` | fresh prefill, 8192 tokens |
+| `32*1@8192` | 32 decodes, KV length 8192 (KV length **includes** the query) |
+| `4@4096:3` | spec-decode verify, 3 draft tokens |
+| `2048@10240` | prefill after an 8192-token prefix-cache hit |
+| `2048@10240c` | chunked prefill: the prefix came from earlier chunks |
+
+Hit vs chunk only differs on models with SWA bounded replay (DSV4.1): a hit
+also recomputes the last window (128 tokens) of the prefix.
+
+Or `--shapes file.json|yaml`:
+`{"cases": [{"name": ..., "requests": [{"query_len", "kv_len", "num_draft_tokens", "chunked", "count"}]}]}`.
+
+Key flags (plus all `EngineArgs`):
+
+- `--kv-len-jitter 0.5` (default): prefixes drawn within ±50%, same on every
+  DP rank, capped at `max_model_len`. Use `0` for exact lengths.
+- `--routing auto|real|balanced`: `auto` = balanced with dummy weights.
+- `--iters 20 --samples 5`, `--output-json out.json` (per-rank latency stats,
+  `samples_us`, graph-vs-eager check).
+- Defaults: `--load-format dummy`, prefix caching off, no torch.compile.
+
+Read `median_us` (each replay is already the max over ranks).
+
+## Caveats
+
+- **Dummy weights lie for data-dependent kernels.** Dummy gates route every
+  token to the same experts (hence balanced routing). Dummy norm weights make
+  DSV4 indexer logits degenerate, so `topKPerRowPrefill` runs ~2.6x slow
+  until #61323 lands. Cross-check suspicious kernels with real weights.
+- **torch.compile models (e.g. Qwen3/3.5) look slow**: no compile here. Use
+  them for correctness only; trust perf for models under `vllm/models/`.
+- `sample spread > 0.5%` warns of unstable timing. DSV4.1 DEP prefill is
+  inherently ~0.5–1% (MegaMoE cross-rank sync, host engram reads).
+- `graph_vs_eager` may be nonzero for small batches where models branch on
+  `is_current_stream_capturing()`; that's expected, not a bug.
+- KV cache is zero-initialized (`--kv-init zeros`); random KV was within 3%.
+- Uniform DP only: every rank gets the same case; no idle ranks.
+- CUDA only: it hangs on ROCm (untested cause: likely the in-graph timing
+  events).
+- Large prefills/prefix hits need room: raise `--max-num-batched-tokens` /
+  `--max-model-len` / `--gpu-memory-utilization` if build fails on KV blocks.
+- Startup cost is JIT/autotune, not the bench: install FlashInfer jit-cache
+  and cubin; DeepGEMM warmup is skipped (each case's eager pass compiles its
+  own shapes).
+- To compare against serving decode: `vllm bench latency` with 65- vs
+  1-token outputs, divided by 64, with a FULL decode graph.

+    groups = [_group(16), _group(32, replay=128)]

+    assert list(batch.expected.values()) == [

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Build a `SchedulerOutput` for an exact batch, without the scheduler."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.benchmarks.forward.shapes import BenchCase
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import NewRequestData, SchedulerOutput
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    CircularBufferSpec,
+    KVCacheSpec,
+    MambaSpec,
+    SlidingWindowSpec,
+    UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class BenchBatch:
+    scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput
+    # req_id -> token IDs of the query tokens, in order.
+    query_token_ids: dict[str, np.ndarray]
+    # Per KV cache group: allocated (begin, end) block ranges.
+    group_block_ranges: list[list[tuple[int, int]]]
+    num_blocks: int
+    # req_id -> the runner's expected (scheduled, computed, is_decode).
+    expected: dict[str, tuple[int, int, bool]]
+
+    @property
+    def num_tokens(self) -> int:
+        return self.scheduler_output.total_num_scheduled_tokens
+
+    @property
+    def req_ids(self) -> list[str]:
+        return list(self.scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens)
+
+    def finish(self) -> SchedulerOutput:
+        """A step that only removes this batch's requests."""
+        output = SchedulerOutput.make_empty()
+        output.finished_req_ids = set(self.req_ids)
+        return output
+
+
+def kv_block_size(spec: KVCacheSpec, dcp_size: int) -> int:
+    """Tokens per block as the scheduler counts them: DCP spreads each
+    block's tokens over the DCP ranks."""
+    return spec.block_size * (dcp_size if spec.dcp_sharded else 1)
+
+
+def _num_blocks(
+    spec: KVCacheSpec, computed: int, kv_len: int, dcp_size: int
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Return (leading null blocks, live blocks) for one request."""
+    block_size = kv_block_size(spec, dcp_size)
+    if isinstance(spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs):
+        spec = spec.first_spec
+    if isinstance(spec, (CircularBufferSpec, MambaSpec)):
+        return 0, 1
+    total = -(-kv_len // block_size)
+    skipped = 0
+    if isinstance(spec, SlidingWindowSpec):
+        # Blocks wholly before the window are freed to the null block.
+        skipped = max(0, computed - spec.sliding_window + 1) // block_size
+    return skipped, total - skipped
+
+
+def build_batch(
+    case: BenchCase,
+    kv_cache_groups,
+    num_kv_blocks: int,
+    vocab_size: int,
+    rng: np.random.Generator,
+    dcp_size: int = 1,
+) -> BenchBatch:
+    """Allocate disjoint blocks and build `NewRequestData` for every request.
+
+    Groups share one block pool, so block IDs are unique across groups. Block
+    0 is the null block.
+
+    With prefix P = K - Q (KV length K, query length Q):
+
+    | Kind               | prompt tokens | num_computed_tokens | spec tokens |
+    | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------- | ----------- |
+    | Prefill            | K             | P                   | -           |
+    | Decode             | P             | P                   | -           |
+    | Verify (D drafts)  | P             | P                   | D           |
+
+    Unless chunked, a prefill's prefix is a prefix hit, which replays its last
+    R = min(window, P) tokens on models with SWA bounded replay (window 0
+    otherwise), like the scheduler: it schedules R + Q tokens from
+    replay_start = num_computed_tokens = P - R.
+    """
+    replay_window = max(
+        (group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_replay_tokens for group in kv_cache_groups),
+        default=0,
+    )
+    expected: dict[str, tuple[int, int, bool]] = {}
+    cursor = 1
+    new_reqs = []
+    query_token_ids = {}
+    group_block_ranges: list[list[tuple[int, int]]] = [[] for _ in kv_cache_groups]
+    output = SchedulerOutput.make_empty()
+    for i, req in enumerate(case.requests):
+        req_id = f"bench-{i}"
+        replay = min(replay_window, req.prefix_len) if req.prefix_hit else 0
+        computed = req.prefix_len - replay
+        block_ids = []
+        for group, ranges in zip(kv_cache_groups, group_block_ranges):
+            skipped, live = _num_blocks(
+                group.kv_cache_spec, computed, req.kv_len, dcp_size
+            )
+            block_ids.append([0] * skipped + list(range(cursor, cursor + live)))
+            ranges.append((cursor, cursor + live))
+            cursor += live
+        tokens = rng.integers(0, vocab_size, req.kv_len, dtype=np.int64)
+        prompt = tokens[: req.prefix_len] if req.is_decode else tokens
+        query_token_ids[req_id] = tokens[computed:]
+        expected[req_id] = (req.query_len + replay, computed, req.is_decode)
+        new_reqs.append(
+            NewRequestData(
+                req_id=req_id,
+                prompt_token_ids=prompt.tolist(),
+                prefill_token_ids=prompt.tolist(),
+                mm_features=[],
+                sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=16, temperature=0.0),
+                pooling_params=None,
+                block_ids=tuple(block_ids),
+                num_computed_tokens=computed,
+                lora_request=None,
+                replay_start=computed if replay else 0,
+            )
+        )
+        output.num_scheduled_tokens[req_id] = req.query_len + replay
+        if req.num_draft_tokens:
+            output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[req_id] = tokens[
+                req.prefix_len + 1 :
+            ].tolist()
+    if cursor > num_kv_blocks:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Case {case.name!r} needs {cursor} KV blocks, but only "
+            f"{num_kv_blocks} exist. Increase the KV cache size."
+        )
+    output.scheduled_new_reqs = new_reqs
+    output.total_num_scheduled_tokens = sum(output.num_scheduled_tokens.values())
+    return BenchBatch(output, query_token_ids, group_block_ranges, cursor, expected)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Capture the forward of one exact batch as a one-shot CUDA graph and time it.
+
+The graph is captured for a single batch and only replays that batch, so the
+host-side decisions baked in at capture (attention plans, kernel choices by
+query length, chunk splits) are correct by construction. This deliberately
+bypasses vLLM's CUDA graph manager: no capture sizes, padding or dummy
+metadata. Each replay first restores the KV blocks the step writes, so state the
+forward mutates in place (e.g. compressor state) is the same on every replay.
+"""
+
+import time
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.benchmarks.forward.batch import BenchBatch
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_world_group, graph_capture
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch
+
+
+def _first_tensor(output: Any) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if isinstance(output, tuple):
+        output = output[0]
+    assert isinstance(output, torch.Tensor), type(output)
+    return output
+
+
+def _compare(actual: torch.Tensor, expected: torch.Tensor) -> dict[str, float]:
+    delta = actual.float() - expected.float()
+    scale = expected.float().square().mean().sqrt().clamp(min=1e-12)
+    return {
+        "max_abs": delta.abs().max().item(),
+        "relative_rms": (delta.square().mean().sqrt() / scale).item(),
+    }
+
+
+class ForwardBench:
+    """Runs one batch through the runner's `execute_model`, timing its forward.
+
+    `execute_model` prepares the inputs, attention metadata and forward context
+    as in serving; the bench takes over the eager model call. Two steps: the
+    first ("warmup") runs the model eagerly, which triggers JIT, autotuning and
+    lazy init. The second ("capture") captures, validates and times the graph.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        runner: Any,
+        batch: BenchBatch,
+        iters: int,
+        samples: int,
+        state_views: list[torch.Tensor],
+    ):
+        self.runner = runner
+        self.batch = batch
+        self.device = runner.device
+        self.iters = iters
+        self.samples = samples
+        self.state_views = state_views
+        self.phase = "warmup"
+        self.result: dict[str, Any] = {}
+
+    def run(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        runner, model = self.runner, self.runner.model
+        # The runner's eager branch calls `model(**inputs)`.
+        assert runner.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode == CUDAGraphMode.NONE
+        assert runner.ubatch_runner is None
+        prepare_inputs = runner.prepare_inputs
+        self._model_forward = model.forward
+
+        def prepare_and_check(*args, **kwargs) -> InputBatch:
+            self._input_batch = prepare_inputs(*args, **kwargs)
+            self._check_batch(self._input_batch)
+            return self._input_batch
+
+        # Instance attributes shadow the methods for these two steps only.
+        runner.prepare_inputs = prepare_and_check
+        model.forward = self._forward
+        try:
+            for self.phase in ("warmup", "capture"):
+                runner.execute_model(self.batch.scheduler_output)
+        finally:
+            del runner.prepare_inputs, model.forward
+            # No sample_tokens follows.
+            runner.execute_model_state = None
+        return self.result
+
+    def _forward(self, **inputs) -> Any:
+        self._write_input_ids(self._input_batch, inputs["input_ids"])
+        # Models may update the forward context in place (e.g. sequence
+        # parallelism shards is_padding); every call must start from the
+        # context the runner built.
+        context = get_forward_context()
+        saved = dict(vars(context))
+
+        def run_model() -> Any:
+            for name, value in saved.items():
+                setattr(context, name, value)
+            return self._model_forward(**inputs)
+
+        self._run_model = run_model
+        if self.phase == "warmup":
+            return run_model()
+        return self._capture_and_time()
+
+    def _check_batch(self, input_batch: InputBatch) -> None:
+        """Fail unless the runner built exactly the requested batch."""
+        expected = self.batch.expected
+        assert sorted(input_batch.req_ids) == sorted(expected), input_batch.req_ids
+        for i, req_id in enumerate(input_batch.req_ids):
+            actual = (
+                int(input_batch.num_scheduled_tokens[i]),
+                int(input_batch.num_computed_tokens_np[i]),
+                not bool(input_batch.is_prefilling_np[i]),
+            )
+            assert actual == expected[req_id], (
+                f"{req_id}: got (scheduled, computed, decode) = {actual}, "
+                f"wanted {expected[req_id]}"
+            )
+        assert input_batch.num_tokens == self.batch.num_tokens
+        self.result["num_tokens_after_padding"] = input_batch.num_tokens_after_padding
+        self.result["batch_order"] = input_batch.req_ids
+
+    def _write_input_ids(
+        self, input_batch: InputBatch, input_ids: torch.Tensor | None
+    ) -> None:
+        """Decode/verify inputs otherwise come from sampler state."""
+        if input_ids is None:
+            return
+        ids = np.concatenate(
+            [self.batch.query_token_ids[req_id] for req_id in input_batch.req_ids]
+        )
+        input_ids[: len(ids)].copy_(torch.from_numpy(ids))
+
+    def _capture_and_time(self) -> Any:
+        world = get_world_group()
+        # The forward mutates state it reads (e.g. compressor state), so
+        # every run starts by restoring the KV blocks the step writes.
+        snapshots = [(view, view.clone()) for view in self.state_views]
+
+        def restore() -> None:
+            for view, saved in snapshots:
+                view.copy_(saved)
+
+        # A rendezvous and the timing events live inside the graph, after the
+        # restore: neither rank skew, the restore nor host launch gaps reach
+        # the timed interval.
+        flag = torch.zeros(1, device=self.device)
+        self._events = (
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True, external=True),
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True, external=True),
+        )
+        if world.world_size > 1:
+            # Initialize the communicator outside capture.
+            torch.distributed.all_reduce(flag, group=world.device_group)
+        with graph_capture(self.device) as capture_context:
+            stream = capture_context.stream
+            # Some kernels set up per-stream state on first use, outside capture.
+            eager = _first_tensor(self._run_model()).clone()
+            restore()
+            reference = _first_tensor(self._run_model()).clone()
+            stream.synchronize()
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+                restore()
+                if world.world_size > 1:
+                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(flag, group=world.device_group)
+                self._events[0].record()
+                output = self._run_model()
+                self._events[1].record()
+        hidden = _first_tensor(output)
+
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        first = hidden.clone()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        self.result.update(
+            # Same step from the same restored state: should match exactly.
+            eager_repeat=_compare(reference, eager),
+            graph_vs_eager=_compare(first, reference),
+            graph_deterministic=bool(torch.equal(first, hidden)),
+            finite=bool(hidden.isfinite().all()),
+            state_reset_bytes=sum(
+                v.numel() * v.element_size() for v in self.state_views
+            ),
+        )
+        self.result["latency_us"] = self._time(graph)
+        del graph
+        return output
+
+    def _time(self, graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Per-replay forward time between in-graph events, MAX across ranks."""
+        world = get_world_group()
+        start, end = self._events
+        self._warmup(graph)
+        times = []
+        for _ in range(self.iters * self.samples):
+            graph.replay()
+            end.synchronize()
+            times.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000)
+        arr = torch.tensor(times, device=self.device)
+        if world.world_size > 1:
+            torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+                arr, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX, group=world.device_group
+            )
+        arr = arr.cpu().numpy()
+        sample_medians = np.median(arr.reshape(self.samples, -1), axis=1)
+        median = float(np.median(arr))
+        return {
+            "timer": "graph_events" + ("_rank_max" if world.world_size > 1 else ""),
+            "median": median,
+            # Stability: spread of per-sample medians relative to the median.
+            "sample_spread_pct": float(
+                100 * (sample_medians.max() - sample_medians.min()) / median
+            ),
+            "mean": float(arr.mean()),
+            "std": float(arr.std()),
+            "min": float(arr.min()),
+            "p90": float(np.percentile(arr, 90)),
+            "count": len(arr),
+            "samples_us": [round(float(t), 2) for t in arr],
+        }
+
+    def _warmup(self, graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph, seconds: float = 1.0) -> None:
+        """Replay until clocks and caches reach a steady state."""
+        world = get_world_group()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        begin = time.perf_counter()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        per_replay = max(time.perf_counter() - begin, 1e-6)
+        # Same count on every rank: the graph may contain collectives.
+        count = torch.tensor([max(self.iters, int(seconds / per_replay))])
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+            count, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX, group=world.cpu_group
+        )
+        for _ in range(int(count.item())):
+            graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""KV blocks of a benchmark case: initialization and the blocks a step writes.
+
+Only the case's blocks are touched, group by group: groups can alias one
+allocation with different layouts, and the batch builder keeps their block IDs
+disjoint. Zero KV times within a few percent of random KV, even for sparse
+attention (DeepSeek-V4.1, ~100K context), so zeros are the only init for now.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.benchmarks.forward.batch import BenchBatch, kv_block_size
+
+
+def _tensors(kv_cache) -> Iterator[torch.Tensor]:
+    if isinstance(kv_cache, torch.Tensor):
+        if kv_cache.numel():
+            yield kv_cache
+    elif isinstance(kv_cache, (list, tuple)):
+        for item in kv_cache:
+            yield from _tensors(item)
+
+
+def _block_dim(tensor: torch.Tensor, num_blocks: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Return (block dim, kernel blocks per allocator block)."""
+    for dim in range(min(2, tensor.dim())):
+        if tensor.shape[dim] >= num_blocks and tensor.shape[dim] % num_blocks == 0:
+            return dim, tensor.shape[dim] // num_blocks
+    raise ValueError(f"No block dim of size {num_blocks} in {tuple(tensor.shape)}")
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def zero_kv_blocks(
+    static_forward_context: dict, kv_cache_groups, batch: BenchBatch, num_blocks: int
+) -> None:
+    for group, ranges in zip(kv_cache_groups, batch.group_block_ranges):
+        for name in group.layer_names:
+            layer = static_forward_context[name]
+            for tensor in _tensors(getattr(layer, "kv_cache", None)):
+                dim, factor = _block_dim(tensor, num_blocks)
+                for begin, end in ranges:
+                    tensor.narrow(dim, begin * factor, (end - begin) * factor).zero_()
+
+
+def touched_kv_views(
+    static_forward_context: dict,
+    kv_cache_groups,
+    batch: BenchBatch,
+    num_blocks: int,
+    dcp_size: int,
+) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """Views of the KV blocks a step may write: each request's last
+    ceil(scheduled / block_size) + 2 blocks, in every group."""
+    scheduled_tokens = [batch.expected[req_id][0] for req_id in batch.req_ids]
+    views = []
+    for group, ranges in zip(kv_cache_groups, batch.group_block_ranges):
+        block_size = kv_block_size(group.kv_cache_spec, dcp_size)
+        for name in group.layer_names:
+            layer = static_forward_context[name]
+            for tensor in _tensors(getattr(layer, "kv_cache", None)):
+                dim, factor = _block_dim(tensor, num_blocks)
+                for (begin, end), tokens in zip(ranges, scheduled_tokens):
+                    first = max(begin, end - (-(-tokens // block_size) + 2))
+                    views.append(
+                        tensor.narrow(dim, first * factor, (end - first) * factor)
+                    )
+    return views

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Benchmark the model forward of exact batches as one-shot CUDA graphs.
+
+Each case is a list of requests `(query_len, kv_len, num_draft_tokens)`
+per DP rank. The bench builds the batch without the scheduler, runs it through
+the real `execute_model` (input prep, attention metadata, DP sync), and times
+the target-model forward captured as a CUDA graph. Sampling, the speculator
+and CPU step overhead aren't measured.
+
+Single GPU: `vllm bench forward --model M --case decode=32*1@8192`.
+Multi-GPU: `torchrun --nproc-per-node=N -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench
+forward ...`, one process per GPU.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import socket
+from dataclasses import asdict
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.benchmarks.forward.shapes import (
+    BenchCase,
+    jitter_kv_lens,
+    load_cases,
+    parse_case,
+)
+from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def add_cli_args(parser: FlexibleArgumentParser) -> None:
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--case",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        help="`NAME=REQS`, where REQS is a comma list of `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` "
+        "(query length Q, KV length K including the query (default Q), D draft "
+        "tokens, N requests). A prefill's prefix is a prefix-cache hit unless c "
+        "marks a chunked prefill. E.g. `decode=32*1@8192`, "
+        "`verify=16*4@4096:3`, `prefill=8192`, `hit=2048@10240`, "
+        "`mix=8192,32*1@8192`. Repeatable.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--shapes", help="JSON or YAML file with cases.")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--kv-len-jitter",
+        type=float,
+        default=0.5,
+        help="Draw each request's prefix (KV length minus query length) "
+        "uniformly within +-this fraction of its value, like the varied lengths "
+        "of a real batch, capped at the max model length. Seeded by --seed only, "
+        "so every DP rank gets the same lengths. 0 keeps the exact lengths.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--kv-init",
+        choices=["zeros"],
+        default="zeros",
+        help="Initial KV cache contents of each case's blocks.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--routing",
+        choices=["auto", "real", "balanced"],
+        default="auto",
+        help="MoE routing. balanced: fixed routing with equal load per EP rank. "
+        "auto: balanced with dummy weights, else real.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=20, help="Replays per sample.")
+    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-json", help="Write results to this file.")
+    EngineArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
+    parser.set_defaults(load_format="dummy", enable_prefix_caching=False)
+
+
+def _setup_env() -> None:
+    os.environ["VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER"] = "1"
+    os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
+    # Each case's eager pass compiles exactly the shapes it needs.
+    os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP", "skip")
+    if "RANK" in os.environ:
+        return  # Launched by torchrun.
+    with socket.socket() as s:
+        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        port = s.getsockname()[1]
+    os.environ.update(
+        RANK="0",
+        LOCAL_RANK="0",
+        WORLD_SIZE="1",
+        MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1",
+        MASTER_PORT=str(port),
+    )
+
+
+def _register_dummy_loader() -> str:
+    """Dummy loader that also runs load-time model finalization.
+
+    TODO(woosuk): Remove once #60096 lands. DeepSeek-V4.1 fuses its MegaMoE
+    shared experts at the end of `load_weights`, before the generic linear
+    post-processing repacks their scales. Dummy loading never calls
+    `load_weights`, so the fusion would fail and the bench would time unfused
+    shared experts.
+    """
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import register_model_loader
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.dummy_loader import DummyModelLoader
+
+    name = "forward_bench_dummy"
+
+    @register_model_loader(name)
+    class ForwardBenchDummyLoader(DummyModelLoader):
+        def load_weights(self, model, model_config) -> None:
+            super().load_weights(model, model_config)
+            if any(hasattr(m, "finalize_mega_moe_weights") for m in model.modules()):
+                model.process_weights_after_loading()
+
+    return name
+
+
+def _make_engine_args(args: argparse.Namespace, cases: list[BenchCase]):
+    from vllm.config.compilation import CompilationMode, CUDAGraphMode
+
+    engine_args = EngineArgs.from_cli_args(args)
+    if engine_args.load_format == "dummy":
+        engine_args.load_format = _register_dummy_loader()
+    engine_args.distributed_executor_backend = "external_launcher"
+    engine_args.enable_prefix_caching = False
+    engine_args.compilation_config.mode = CompilationMode.NONE
+    engine_args.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.NONE
+    if engine_args.max_num_seqs is None:
+        engine_args.max_num_seqs = max(len(c.requests) for c in cases)
+    if engine_args.max_num_batched_tokens is None:
+        # Prefix hits may replay up to a window more per request.
+        engine_args.max_num_batched_tokens = max(
+            8192,
+            *(
+                c.num_tokens + 1024 * sum(r.prefix_hit for r in c.requests)
+                for c in cases
+            ),
+        )
+    return engine_args
+
+
+def run_case(runner, case: BenchCase, args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    from vllm.benchmarks.forward.batch import build_batch
+    from vllm.benchmarks.forward.capture import ForwardBench
+    from vllm.benchmarks.forward.kv_init import touched_kv_views, zero_kv_blocks
+    from vllm.benchmarks.forward.routing import install_routing
+
+    context = runner.vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context
+    kv_config = runner.kv_cache_config
+    dcp_size = runner.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size
+    rng = np.random.default_rng([args.seed, runner.dp_rank])
+    batch = build_batch(
+        case,
+        kv_config.kv_cache_groups,
+        kv_config.num_blocks,
+        runner.model_config.get_vocab_size(),
+        rng,
+        dcp_size,
+    )
+    zero_kv_blocks(context, kv_config.kv_cache_groups, batch, kv_config.num_blocks)
+    bench = ForwardBench(
+        runner,
+        batch,
+        args.iters,
+        args.samples,
+        touched_kv_views(
+            context, kv_config.kv_cache_groups, batch, kv_config.num_blocks, dcp_size
+        ),
+    )
+    routing, balanced = install_routing(
+        runner, args.routing, args.load_format == "dummy", batch.num_tokens, args.seed
+    )
+    try:
+        result = bench.run()
+        if balanced is not None:
+            balanced.check_applied()
+    finally:
+        runner.execute_model(batch.finish())
+        if balanced is not None:
+            balanced.remove()
+    return {
+        "num_tokens": batch.num_tokens,
+        "kv_blocks": batch.num_blocks,
+        "routing": routing,
+        **result,
+    }
+
+
+def main(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+    cases = [parse_case(c) for c in args.case]
+    if args.shapes:
+        cases += load_cases(args.shapes)
+    if not cases:
+        raise ValueError("Pass at least one --case or --shapes.")
+    if not 0 <= args.kv_len_jitter < 1:
+        raise ValueError("--kv-len-jitter must be in [0, 1).")
+    _setup_env()
+
+    from vllm import LLM
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_world_group
+
+    llm = LLM.from_engine_args(_make_engine_args(args, cases))
+    runner = llm.llm_engine.model_executor.driver_worker.worker.model_runner
+    # Same draw on every rank: shapes are balanced across DP ranks.
+    max_kv_len = runner.model_config.max_model_len
+    cases = [
+        jitter_kv_lens(c, args.kv_len_jitter, max_kv_len, args.seed) for c in cases
+    ]
+    world = get_world_group()
+    results = []
+    with torch.inference_mode(), set_current_vllm_config(runner.vllm_config):
+        for case in cases:
+            result = run_case(runner, case, args)
+            gathered: list[Any] = [None] * world.world_size
+            torch.distributed.all_gather_object(gathered, result, group=world.cpu_group)
+            if world.rank != 0:
+                continue
+            rank0 = gathered[0]
+            latency = rank0["latency_us"]  # Each replay is the max over ranks.
+            results.append(
+                {
+                    "case": case.name,
+                    "requests": [asdict(r) for r in case.requests],
+                    "median_us": latency["median"],
+                    "ranks": gathered,
+                }
+            )
+            print(
+                f"[forward] {case.name}: {len(case.requests)} reqs, "
+                f"{rank0['num_tokens']} tokens, median {latency['median']:.1f} us, "
+                f"sample spread {latency['sample_spread_pct']:.2f}%, graph vs "
+                f"eager rel rms {rank0['graph_vs_eager']['relative_rms']:.1e}",
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            if latency["sample_spread_pct"] > 0.5:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "%s: unstable timing (sample medians spread %.2f%%).",
+                    case.name,
+                    latency["sample_spread_pct"],
+                )
+    if world.rank == 0 and args.output_json:
+        with open(args.output_json, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Balanced MoE routing for benchmarks with dummy weights.
+
+Dummy gate weights give degenerate routing, which skews MoE and all-to-all
+cost. The routing still runs; its result is replaced by the fixture at
+whichever boundary the layer exposes:
+
+- Gate output: fixed logits whose top-k is the fixture. Covers every backend
+  that routes from logits, including monolithic kernels that run top-k
+  internally (e.g. FlashInfer TRTLLM).
+- Experts input: models that compute top-k themselves and pass
+  `topk_ids` to their experts (e.g. MegaMoE with a fused gate) get the
+  fixture's IDs. The routing weights are kept; they don't affect cost.
+
+Hash-routed layers ignore logits and keep their tables unless their experts
+take `topk_ids`.
+"""
+
+import inspect
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.gate_linear import GateLinear
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# Fixture logits: chosen experts score far above the rest under any monotonic
+# scoring function, so top-k picks exactly them.
+_CHOSEN_LOGIT = 4.0
+_OTHER_LOGIT = -4.0
+
+
+def balanced_topk_ids(
+    num_tokens: int, num_experts: int, top_k: int, ep_size: int, rng
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Expert IDs [num_tokens, top_k] giving every EP rank equal load.
+
+    Each token's slots go round-robin over EP ranks, to distinct experts.
+    """
+    assert num_experts % ep_size == 0
+    local = num_experts // ep_size
+    slots = np.arange(num_tokens)[:, None] * top_k + np.arange(top_k)
+    ranks = slots % ep_size
+    # Slots of one token that land on the same rank take consecutive experts.
+    repeat = np.zeros_like(ranks)
+    for j in range(1, top_k):
+        repeat[:, j] = (ranks[:, :j] == ranks[:, j : j + 1]).sum(axis=1)
+    assert repeat.max() < local
+    base = rng.integers(local, size=(num_tokens, ep_size))
+    offset = np.take_along_axis(base, ranks, axis=1)
+    return ranks * local + (offset + repeat) % local
+
+
+def _moe_layers(model: torch.nn.Module) -> list[tuple[torch.nn.Module, GateLinear]]:
+    """(MoE module, gate) per layer, in model order."""
+    layers: dict[GateLinear, torch.nn.Module] = {}
+    for module in model.modules():
+        gate = getattr(module, "gate", None)
+        if not isinstance(gate, GateLinear) or gate in layers:
+            continue
+        if _top_k(module) is not None:
+            layers[gate] = module
+    return [(module, gate) for gate, module in layers.items()]
+
+
+def _top_k(module: torch.nn.Module) -> int | None:
+    """The MoE layer's top-k, from the module or its experts submodules."""
+    for sub in module.modules():
+        for name in ("top_k", "n_activated_experts"):
+            top_k = getattr(sub, name, None)
+            if isinstance(top_k, int):
+                return top_k
+    return None
+
+
+class BalancedRouting:
+    """Installs balanced routing for one case; `remove()` restores the model."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model: torch.nn.Module,
+        num_tokens: int,
+        dp_rank: int,
+        dp_size: int,
+        ep_size: int,
+        seed: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ):
+        layers = _moe_layers(model)
+        if not layers:
+            raise ValueError("No MoE gates found; use --routing real.")
+        self._hooks = []
+        self._biases: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = []
+        self._fired = [0] * len(layers)
+        self._layers = layers
+        # Per-rank rows, with headroom for padding; every rank generates the
+        # same global fixture and takes its slice.
+        rows = -(-num_tokens // 256) * 256 + 256
+        for layer, (module, gate) in enumerate(layers):
+            if (getattr(module, "num_expert_group", None) or 1) > 1:
+                raise NotImplementedError("Balanced routing with grouped top-k.")
+            num_experts = gate.weight.shape[0]
+            top_k = _top_k(module)
+            assert top_k is not None
+            rng = np.random.default_rng([seed, layer])
+            ids = balanced_topk_ids(rows * dp_size, num_experts, top_k, ep_size, rng)[
+                dp_rank * rows : (dp_rank + 1) * rows
+            ]
+            logits = torch.full((rows, num_experts), _OTHER_LOGIT, dtype=torch.float32)
+            logits.scatter_(1, torch.from_numpy(ids), _CHOSEN_LOGIT)
+            # Distinct values: no ties for any top-k implementation.
+            logits += torch.from_numpy(rng.uniform(0, 0.5, logits.shape)).float()
+            self._hooks.append(
+                gate.register_forward_hook(
+                    self._substitute(logits.to(device), self._fired, layer)
+                )
+            )
+            bias = getattr(gate, "e_score_correction_bias", None)
+            if bias is None:
+                bias = getattr(module, "e_score_correction_bias", None)
+            if isinstance(bias, torch.Tensor):
+                self._biases.append((bias, bias.detach().clone()))
+                bias.data.zero_()
+            experts = getattr(module, "experts", None)
+            if isinstance(experts, torch.nn.Module):
+                params = list(inspect.signature(experts.forward).parameters)
+                if "topk_ids" in params:
+                    self._hooks.append(
+                        experts.register_forward_pre_hook(
+                            self._substitute_ids(
+                                torch.from_numpy(ids).to(device),
+                                params.index("topk_ids"),
+                                self._fired,
+                                layer,
+                            ),
+                            with_kwargs=True,
+                        )
+                    )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _substitute(fixture: torch.Tensor, fired: list[int], layer: int):
+        cast = [fixture]
+
+        def hook(module, inputs, output):
+            fired[layer] += 1
+            logits = output[0] if isinstance(output, tuple) else output
+            if cast[0].dtype != logits.dtype:
+                cast[0] = fixture.to(logits.dtype)  # Once, at warmup.
+            replaced = cast[0][: logits.shape[0]]
+            return (replaced, *output[1:]) if isinstance(output, tuple) else replaced
+
+        return hook
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _substitute_ids(fixture: torch.Tensor, index: int, fired, layer: int):
+        cast = [fixture]
+
+        def hook(module, args, kwargs):
+            fired[layer] += 1
+            ids = kwargs["topk_ids"] if "topk_ids" in kwargs else args[index]
+            if cast[0].dtype != ids.dtype:
+                cast[0] = fixture.to(ids.dtype)  # Once, at warmup.
+            replaced = cast[0][: ids.shape[0]]
+            if "topk_ids" in kwargs:
+                return args, {**kwargs, "topk_ids": replaced}
+            return (*args[:index], replaced, *args[index + 1 :]), kwargs
+
+        return hook
+
+    def check_applied(self) -> None:
+        """Fail if a layer bypassed both the gate and the experts hooks."""
+        missed = [
+            type(module).__name__
+            for (module, _), fired in zip(self._layers, self._fired)
+            if not fired
+        ]
+        if missed:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Balanced routing didn't reach {len(missed)} MoE layers "
+                f"({missed[0]}): their gate is fused away. Use --routing real."
+            )
+
+    def remove(self) -> None:
+        for hook in self._hooks:
+            hook.remove()
+        for bias, saved in self._biases:
+            bias.data.copy_(saved)
+
+
+def install_routing(
+    runner, requested: str, dummy_weights: bool, num_tokens: int, seed: int
+) -> tuple[str, BalancedRouting | None]:
+    """Resolve `--routing` and install balanced routing if selected.
+
+    `auto` is balanced with dummy weights and real otherwise; it falls back to
+    real routing when the model doesn't support the fixture.
+    """
+    mode = requested
+    if mode == "auto":
+        mode = "balanced" if dummy_weights else "real"
+    if mode == "real":
+        return mode, None
+    parallel = runner.parallel_config
+    ep_size = (
+        parallel.data_parallel_size * parallel.tensor_parallel_size
+        if parallel.enable_expert_parallel
+        else 1
+    )
+    try:
+        routing = BalancedRouting(
+            runner.model,
+            num_tokens,
+            runner.dp_rank,
+            runner.dp_size,
+            ep_size,
+            seed,
+            runner.device,
+        )
+    except (ValueError, NotImplementedError) as e:
+        if requested == "balanced":
+            raise
+        logger.warning("Using real routing: %s", e)
+        return "real", None
+    return mode, routing
